about.title: About Me
about.path_description: Project manager at the French Ministry of Ecological Transition, I lead Aidy: a RAG-based AI assistant deployed to 2,500 staff for access to HR documentation. I work across the whole chain, from designing the CI/CD pipelines to semantic chunking of the corpora and the MCP architecture connecting APIs to the assistants. Specialised in business analysis and change management, I build the solution as much as I drive its adoption: that is where the difference lies between a tool delivered and a tool actually used.
about.method_intro: Four principles that come back on every mission, whatever the subject.

listen.title: I start by listening
listen.desc: I don't turn down a mission on principle, but I won't commit to anything before I understand the context: who will use the tool day to day, what has already been tried, where it actually breaks down. The real friction is rarely in the original specification.

translate.title: I translate in both directions
translate.desc: Business teams and technical teams rarely describe the same problem in the same words. My job is to hold both in one shared document, and to keep it current as the project moves.

reluctant.title: I design for the most reluctant
reluctant.desc: Training built for the people already comfortable with the tool only widens the gap. If the material works for the most resistant person on the team, it works for everyone. That is the subject of my thesis — and the idea behind the "Aa / Dys" button at the bottom of this site, which switches to a typeface and contrast built for reading difficulties.

adoption.title: A project isn't finished when it ships
adoption.desc: It is finished when it is used. I put adoption indicators in place from the start, to know whether the tool has found its place or whether the support needs another pass.
